The Supreme Court has clarified that the Delhi government and various state governments are free to close or withdraw FIRs registered against protesters involved in the recent student protests at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar and elsewhere in the country.A three-judge Bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant explained that its 28th of July order permitting the prosecution of protesters with “criminal antecedents” was intended to apply only to those accused of grave and heinous offences. The top court was hearing pleas alleging excessive police action against students who participated in protests at Jantar Mantar on 20th of July and at other places across the country over the NEET examination paper leak issue. Families of injured police officers had also approached the top court seeking action against protesters for allegedly assaulting police personnel.As the hearing commenced, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, told the top court that while the government stood by its assurance to facilitate the withdrawal of cases against students, there was some confusion over the legal terminology. He explained that criminal law does not provide for the withdrawal of an FIR as such. Instead, the appropriate legal course would be to file a closure report, move an application to withdraw the prosecution, or seek quashing of the proceedings before the competent court.In response, Chief Justice Surya Kant said the court would lay down a protocol governing the circumstances and manner in which pellet guns may be used. The Bench also said it was considering the formation of a Special Investigation Team (SIT) comprising police officers to investigate the allegations of police excesses, or alternatively, the appointment of a committee headed by a retired judge. The apex court posted the matter for further hearing on 18th of August.

. At the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, India’s medal hunt enters the final day with judo and track cycling offering the last opportunities to add to the tally. Avtar Singh in the men’s 100kg, Yash Ghangas in the men’s +100kg and Ishroop Narang in the women’s 78kg category will lead India’s judo challenge, while Ronaldo Laitonjam will compete in the men’s 1,000-metre time trial in track cycling. Para track cycling events are also scheduled on the closing day.India climbed to fourth place in the Commonwealth Games 2026 medal standings in Glasgow following a remarkable Day 10, securing 16 medals on Saturday. This surge brought India’s tally to 39 medals, comprising 13 gold, 17 silver, and 9 bronze, with the boxing contingent leading the charge.India finished atop the boxing medal table, achieving its best-ever performance at the Commonwealth Games with a record seven gold and three silver medals. Among the gold medallists, Ankush Panghal defeated England’s Dimeji Shittu 4-1 in the men’s 80kg final, while Sachin Siwach edged past Namibia’s Tryagain Morning Ndevelo 3-2 to claim the men’s 60kg title. The other Indian boxing gold medallists included Jaismine Lamboria, Preeti Pawar, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, and Arundhati Choudhary.Three Indian boxers, Narender Berwal, Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain, and Jadumani Singh, settled for silver medals. Narender lost to England’s Damar Thomas by a unanimous decision in the men’s 90+kg final. Lovlina went down 4-1 to Australia’s Emma-Sue Greentree in the women’s 75kg final. Preeti claimed the women’s 54-kilogram boxing title with a commanding 5-0 victory over Canada’s Scarlett Delgado. Jaismine, the reigning world champion, secured another 5-0 win in the women’s 57-kilogram final, defeating Michaela Walsh of Northern Ireland.Sakshi then beat Ruby White of England in the women’s 51-kilogram final 5-0 to win. It was a harder final bout for Priya, who beat Marie-Bathoul Al-Ahmadieh of Canada 4-1 in a split verdict in the women’s 60-kilogram final. Arundhati Choudhary also defeated Chantelle Reid of England in the women’s 70-kilogram final.Long-distance runner Gulveer Singh has scripted history at the Commonwealth Games, winning bronze in the men’s 5,000 metres after a silver in the 10,000 metres. He becomes the first Indian track and field athlete to win two medals in a single edition of the Games and the first Indian to claim a Commonwealth medal in the 5,000 metres. The reigning Asian champion clocked 13 minutes 24.95 seconds to complete a historic double.India also celebrated a historic achievement in para-athletics, with Soman Rana winning gold and Shubham Juyal taking silver in the men’s shot put F57 event. This result marked India’s first-ever Commonwealth Games gold medal in the men’s shot put F57 event and the nation’s first double podium finish in the category.In the men’s triple jump event, Praveen Chithravel won silver, while Selva Prabhu Thirumaran clinched bronze. On the judo mat, Unnati Sharma clinched the women’s 63kg bronze medal after defeating Skye Knoester of South Africa by Ippon in the third-place contest. Karanjit Singh Maan reached the men’s -90kg quarter-finals with an ippon win over New Zealand’s Elliott Connolly before suffering defeats to Canada’s Guillaume Gaulin in the last eight and Scotland’s Scott Cuscak in the repechage.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended in positive zone for the fourth straight session today. The Sensex rose 544 points or 0.7 percent to close at 78,639. The Nifty surged 391 points or 1.6 percent to settle at 24,774.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index jumped 1.2% and the Smallcap 100 index gained 1.3%.In the Sensex pack, 21 out of 30 companies registered gains. Among the top performers, Indigo climbed 4.2 per cent, Tata Consultancy Services rose 3.6 per cent and Infosys added 3.5%. In contrast, SunPharma shed two per cent, Bharti Airtel as well as Maruti dipped 1% and Tata steel lost 0.4 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 26 out of 28 sectors ended in positive zone. Among the top gainers, IT as well as Focused IT advanced 2.7%, Services rose 2% and Industrials gained 1.3 %. In contrast, Hospitals lost 0.6%and Healtcare dipped 0.2%.The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 2837 companies advanced, 1552 declined, and 206 remained unchanged.

. In the Indian bullion market, 24 carat Gold was trading marginally up at 1,43,520 rupees per 10 grams, while Silver was also trading marginally up at 2,18,330 rupees per kilogram, a short while ago.On the Multi Commodity Exchange, Gold for the August contract was trading 0.2 per cent up at 1,41,797 rupees per 10 grams, and Silver for the September contract was trading 0.2 per cent up at 2,176,09 rupees per kilogram, when reports last came in.
. In the forex market today, the rupee appreciated by five paise to end at 95 rupees and 34 paise against the US dollar.

. The Second Meeting of the BRICS Anti-Corruption Working Group and the BRICS Expert Network on Asset Recovery will begin in Hyderabad, Telangana, today. The two-day meeting is being organized in line with the theme of India’s BRICS Presidency, Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. Secretary, Department of Personnel and Training, Rachna Shah, will inaugurate the meeting.The event is expected to witness participation from BRICS member countries, along with senior policymakers, experts, practitioners and representatives of anti-corruption and law enforcement agencies. During the meeting, BRICS members will deliberate on strengthening international cooperation for asset recovery, combating cross-border corruption, and enhancing transparency and accountability in governance. The Hyderabad meeting builds upon the outcomes of the First BRICS Anti-Corruption Working Group Meeting held virtually in June.

. Iran said today there were no talks under ​way with the United States and no plans for any meetings, contradicting U.S. President Donald Trump who had said that negotiations with Iran through intermediaries are scheduled to take place today. Speaking to reporters on board Air Force One, Mr. Trump had said that diplomatic engagements involving Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Iran led him to halt what was originally planned as a massive attack. However, Iran’s Foreign ⁠Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei rejected the claim, saying no negotiations with the United States were taking place and no meetings were scheduled. Baghaei added that all Iranian negotiators were ​currently in the country, apart from Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi, who was on a religious pilgrimage in Iraq. The only talks under way, he said, were discussions with Oman over management of the Strait of Hormuz.

. The situation in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoJK) worsened overnight as protesters refused to disperse and security forces allegedly opened fire on demonstrators. Reports from PoJK said that the security forces launched a midnight crackdown on protesters, with gunfire reported in Rawalakot.An Intelligence Bureau official said the reported gunfire came as scores of women and children joined the ongoing protest. Many women and children have remained at the protest site for the past 50 days, with dozens more joining them yesterday.  People from across PoJK have joined the agitation, which is now spreading rapidly across the region.  According to data updated by the Human Rights Council of Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir as of yesterday, a total of 80 fatalities have been documented.The protests began with the people of the region asking for better amenities and more development. Protesters have now announced plans to march to Muzaffarabad to voice their opposition to what they describe as a heavily manipulated election. They allege that Pakistan’s extensive interference in the administration of PoJK has undermined the democratic process and left the region with little or no development.

. Global crude oil prices plunged today after US President Donald Trump held off a fresh attack on Iran as he sought a quick deal that would halt Tehran’s ​nuclear ambitions and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.Brent crude was trading 5.4 per cent down at 83 US dollars and 16 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 6.4 per cent lower at 79 US dollars and 26 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. India and Uzbekistan have agreed to expand their strategic partnership by strengthening cooperation in critical minerals, mining, trade, energy, infrastructure, defence and education during high-level talks held in New Delhi yesterday.The discussions took place during the four-day official visit of Uzbekistan’s Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov, who met External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar.Welcoming the visiting delegation, EAM Jaishankar described Uzbekistan as an important part of India’s extended neighbourhood and highlighted the long-standing historical, cultural and civilisational ties between the two countries.He said bilateral relations have steadily expanded over the years and now cover a wide range of sectors, including construction, digital technology, energy, healthcare and education.The External Affairs Minister said both countries are now looking to broaden cooperation into the mining sector, particularly critical minerals and rare earth resources. Referring to bilateral trade of nearly one billion US dollars, he expressed confidence that economic exchanges would increase significantly in the coming years.EAM Jaishankar said the two sides conducted a comprehensive review of their strategic partnership with particular focus on energy, infrastructure, trade, defence, education and culture. They also discussed regional developments and explored ways to strengthen cooperation in multilateral forums.On foreign policy issues, EAM Jaishankar noted that India and Uzbekistan share similar perspectives on terrorism, extremism and drug trafficking. He appreciated Uzbekistan’s firm stand against terrorism, stating that both countries have consistently maintained a policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism, including cross-border terrorism and terror sanctuaries.The Minister also thanked Uzbekistan for supporting India’s initiatives during its BRICS Presidency in 2026 and conveyed New Delhi’s support for Uzbekistan’s candidature to chair the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) for the 2027-2029 period.Earlier in the day, Saidov called on President Droupadi Murmu at the Rashtrapati Bhavan. During the meeting, President Murmu underscored the deep historical links between the two nations and stressed that the current visit offers an opportunity to identify new areas of cooperation and further strengthen bilateral ties.She highlighted the significant potential for collaboration in mining, particularly rare earth minerals, as well as agriculture, pharmaceuticals and information technology.The President also praised the strong educational and professional exchanges between the two countries, noting that more than 3,000 Uzbek officials, professionals and students have benefited from India’s Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) programme and scholarship schemes.She added that over 16,000 Indian students are currently pursuing higher education in Uzbekistan.

. The India Meteorological Department has forecast extremely heavy rainfall today over parts of Assam, Meghalaya, the Sub-Himalayas, West Bengal and Sikkim. Heavy to very heavy rainfall is also expected today in places over Arunachal Pradesh, Bihar, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura.According to the Met Department parts of Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Jammu and Kashmir, Kerala, Mahe, Himachal Pradesh, Odisha and Uttar Pradesh are also likely to receive moderate to heavy rainfall during the day. IMD also predicted thunderstorm conditions over Andaman and Nicobar Islands today. Similar weather conditions are also expected over Andhra Pradesh, Coastal Karnataka, Kerala and Mahe, Lakshadweep and North Interior Karnataka.

. In Greece, two firefighting helicopters collided in the area of ​Psatha in the Attica region, while helping to control a huge wildfire ​that has destroyed more than 100 homes northwest of Athens. Two people on one helicopter – a Greek and a Danish national ‌died, while the crew on the other, one person from Greece, one from Britain, survived, the fire service said. Investigations had started into what caused the collision.Europe has been ravaged by wildfires this summer after a period of record-breaking heatwaves and little rain, conditions that scientists say have been exacerbated by climate change. Destructive blazes in France and Spain showed some signs of easing over the weekend, but several wildfires have broken out in Greece after a period of relative calm there.

. US President Donald Trump said Iran has been given a last chance to reach an agreement with Washington, claiming that a planned military strike was paused after Iran and several Gulf countries urged diplomacy. Speaking at the Oval Office, Trump said the US was prepared to launch a major attack on Iran but delayed the action after receiving calls from Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, and Iran to continue discussions.Trump also said discussions were underway to reopen the Strait of Hormuz completely, possibly by tomorrow. He described this as the first phase, with the second phase focusing on the denuclearisation of Iran.However, Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei denied reports of direct or indirect negotiations with the US, saying Tehran was not holding talks with Washington. He also said a recent Iran-Oman maritime arrangement was only a technical step for safer ship movement and did not mean the Strait of Hormuz had been reopened.Trump again accused Iran of denying talks publicly while engaging in discussions privately. He repeated that Iran would not be allowed to obtain nuclear weapons. Separately, Trump signed an executive order creating the first-ever Presidential Military Spouse Commission to support military families.

. The countdown to the 2030 Ahmedabad Commonwealth Games has officially begun, with the curtain falling on the Glasgow Commonwealth Games last night. As the curtain came down, India offered the world a vibrant invitation to Ahmedabad, blending ancient philosophy, contemporary artistry and cultural grandeur in a handover presentation that officially launched the journey towards the centenary edition of the Games in 2030.Prince Edward, Duke of Edinburgh, representing King Charles III, formally declared the Games closed in Glasgow. He called up on athletes of all countries and territories to visit Ahmedabad in four years’ time to celebrate the 24th Commonwealth Games.The formal handover began with the Commonwealth Games flag making its symbolic journey across the arena. Led by bearers holding the Scottish and Indian flags, the procession lowered the folded Games flag. Glasgow’s Lord Provost Jacqueline McLaren then passed it to Commonwealth Games Scotland vice-chair Susan Jackson, two-time Olympic medallist Neeraj Chopra, Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha, and finally Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi.This marked the official transfer of hosting responsibilities from Scotland to India. India last hosted the Commonwealth Games in New Delhi in 2010. After 11 days of intense competition, Indian athletes departed from Glasgow as a satisfied bunch after winning 39 medals at the 2026 Games, including 13 gold, 17 silver, and nine bronze, to end in fourth position on the standings.

A delegation from Bastar Mandal of Chhattisgarh comprising winners of Bastar Pandum 2026, Pargana Manjhi and Chalaki of Bastar and Padma awardees, called on President Droupadi Murmu today at Rashtrapati Bhavan Cultural Centre. The President felicitated the members of the delegation and interacted with them. Union Minister for Home Affairs and Cooperation, Amit Shah, and Chief Minister of Chhattisgarh, Vishnu Deo Sai were present on the occasion.Speaking on the occasion, the President emphasized that events like Bastar Pandum have played an important role in reconnecting the youth with their traditions, customs, and cultural heritage. President Murmu highlighted that such events promote tourism and create employment opportunities. The President noted that the transformation in Bastar is a source of joy and pride for the entire nation. She expressed confidence that people of Chhattisgarh will scale new heights of development, peace and prosperity through their collective strength and determination. Further, President Murmu assured them that the government would stand by them in every situation.

. Indian Railways recorded growth of 9 percent in freight loading in July this year as compared to the corresponding month of the previous year. It loaded 141.3 million tonnes of freight during July 2026, compared to 129.7 million tonnes in July last year. The performance reflects sustained demand across core sectors of the economy and continued efforts to improve freight logistics and operational efficiency.Further, Iron Ore loading increased by 22.2 per cent, Coal by 11.5 per cent, Food Grains by 11.5 per cent, Fertilizers by 12 per cent and Balance Other Goods by 12.1 per cent. Indian Railways stepped up domestic coal supply to power plants by 20 percent due to an increase in coal demand at thermal power plants, in July compared to the corresponding month last year.The increase in freight movement resulted in an incremental freight revenue of over one thousand one hundred crore rupees in July 2025, registering an 8 per cent growth. Additionally, Indian Railways carried 63.35 crore passengers during July 2026, compared to 62.19 crore during the corresponding month last year. Passenger traffic continued to grow across both suburban and non-suburban segments, reflecting the growing preference for rail travel across the country.

. Union Textiles Minister Giriraj Singh today emphasized that technology and tradition must progress together to ensure the long term growth of the handloom sector.Addressing the inaugural ceremony of Centre of Excellence in Handloom Technology at Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi, the Minister said that this center will play a pivotal role in bridging traditional crafts and modern technology, enhancing weavers’ productivity, promoting innovation and connecting their products to new markets. He added that the center will support research, skill development and innovation, enabling artisans and weavers to adopt modern techniques without compromising India’s rich weaving heritage. The Minister further underlined the need to develop new and sustainable fibres to meet changing consumer preferences and strengthen the handloom sector.On the occasion, Mr Singh also launched five flagship initiatives, including handloom 4.0, handloom x, handloom e-vidya, Kalagriha handloom studio and Threads of Valour.

. In Pakistan, at least 14 people, including five security men, were killed and over a dozen injured in a suicide attack on a police station during a peace rally in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province yesterday. The explosion occurred when the Swat Peace Rally was in progress right across the police station in Kabal town in Swat district.No group or individual has claimed immediate responsibility for the attack. Nine bodies were shifted to Central Hospital Saidu Sharif, while doctors at Kabal Hospital confirmed five more fatalities, taking the total number of confirmed deaths to 14, a Rescue 1122 Swat spokesperson said.The Swat Peace Rally was organised by Swat Aman Jirga (local tribal council), with participants raising slogans and carrying placards to demand peace in the area. They alleged that police inaction has resulted in deterioration in the security situation in the past few months.According to the District Police Officer of Swat, the suspected suicide bomber attempted to enter the Kabal Police Station and Police Lines compound but was intercepted by police personnel at the main gate. The attacker then detonated the explosive device, damaging the main gate and preventing entry into the heavily secured compound. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Muhammad Suhail Afridi strongly condemned the blast and asked the Inspector General of Police to file a report on the incident.

. In Badminton, India’s Tanvi Sharma claimed her maiden BWF World Tour title, defeating Vietnam’s 6th-seeded Nguyen Thuy Linh 21-16, 21-16 to win the Taipei Open Super women’s singles title today. The 17-year old Tanvi became the youngest Taipei Open champion surpassing Taiwan’s Tai Tzu Ying. She is also the first Indian woman to win the title since Saina Nehwal in 2008.

. Bharatiya Janata Party National President Nitin Nabin has said that the party accepts the mandate received in three assembly by-elections. In a social media post, he expressed gratitude to the people of Manjalpur assembly constituency in Gujarat for expressing their faith in the BJP.He extended congratulations to all the dedicated workers and office-bearers of the BJP for this victory. Mr Nabin said that in Bankipur, Datia, BJP did not receive the expected mandate. He said that the party will conduct a thorough introspection of the election results in both these areas. He added that the party will continue to go among the people and work tirelessly to further strengthen their trust.

. Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Dr. Jitendra Singh today said that sustained institutional reforms, technology-driven governance and continuous monitoring have significantly strengthened the country’s vigilance framework. The minister said this during his meeting with the outgoing Central Vigilance Commissioner, Praveen Kumar Srivastava. Dr Singh said that the framework has led to a sharp reduction in the pendency of disciplinary cases from over 4000 to nearly 700 in about three to four years. He noted that transparent and time-bound vigilance mechanisms are essential for good governance and inspire greater public confidence in institutions. He said that the significant reduction in pending disciplinary cases demonstrates the impact of sustained administrative reforms and closer coordination among Ministries, Departments and vigilance authorities.Mr Srivastava also briefed the Minister on the major initiatives undertaken by the Central Vigilance Commission in recent years to modernise vigilance administration through technology, process reforms and capacity building. The meeting reviewed the Commission’s increasing emphasis on technology-enabled vigilance through initiatives relating to digital governance, fraud prevention in banking and financial institutions, cyber security and ethical use of Artificial Intelligence.

. Union Minister for Development of the North Eastern Region, Jyotiraditya Scindia, today met Commonwealth Games gold medallist Mirabai Chanu in New Delhi and congratulated her on winning a record-extending third consecutive Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow. During the meeting, Mr Scindia lauded Mirabai Chanu’s determination and perseverance, and noted that her achievement will inspire young athletes across the country, particularly in the Northeast. They also discussed various aspects of high-performance sports, including training, nutrition, recovery and athlete support.The Minister highlighted the Centre’s efforts to strengthen the sporting ecosystem in the Northeast through the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region’s High-Level Task Force and the One State, One Sport initiative. He said that the primary focus of the Government is to create world-class coaching, scientific training and sports infrastructure, nurturing more champions from the region.

. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has provided a draft notification proposing an amendment to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, to bring two-wheeled road ambulances for emergency medical care. The Ministry underlined that the proposed emergency ambulance service will support faster emergency response and improve access to emergency medical care in remote areas.The Ministry also issued a draft notification proposing amendments to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, for the phased implementation of Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication systems in motor vehicles. It said that the V2V communication will help to line up crucial information that can provide advance warnings to drivers or vehicle systems in safety-critical situations, including sudden braking, forward-collision risk, unsafe lane changes and the approach of emergency vehicles.

. External Affairs Minister Dr Subrahmanyam Jaishankar has said that India has consistently supported the United Nations in strengthening international peace and security. In a written reply in the Lok Sabha today, Dr Jaishankar said, this support has been expressed in a variety of ways, including its unique contribution to UN peacekeeping operations. He said, this contribution is also reflected in India’s membership of the UN Security Council on eight occasions, with the next candidature formally announced for 2028-29. The Minister said, each tenure has witnessed placing issues of Indian interest on the international agenda, the most recent one, in 2021-22, focusing on maritime security and counter-terrorism. He said, the six priorities for the 2028-29 candidature are, A Voice of Global South, Advancing Reformed Multilateralism, A Future Ready Peacekeeping, Addressing threats posed by the misuse of AI, Securing Maritime Commons and Countering Terror Financing.Dr Jaishankar said India is a key contributor to global peace and security, with almost three lakh peacekeepers serving in more than 50 UN missions. He said, currently, four thousand two hundred Indian peacekeepers are deployed in nine out of 11 active missions, working in challenging conditions to promote international peace. The Minister said, India has firmly advanced its view that dialogue and diplomacy are the best means to achieve lasting and durable peace. He said, this has been stated in respect of the Ukraine conflict, the developments in West Asia as well as hostilities in the Gulf. Dr Jaishankar said, with regard to the challenge of terrorism, India has strongly advocated a policy of zero-tolerance and asserted the right of nations to defend themselves against terrorism. He said, since 1996, India has also called for the adoption of a Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism.

. The National Democratic Alliance (NDA) Parliamentary Party’s weekly strategy meeting, known as Mangal Milan, is underway at the Parliament House. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar and other leaders are attending the meeting. The meetings are traditionally held on Tuesdays during Parliament sessions with an aim to demonstrate complete alliance unity. The meeting last took place on the 28th of July. MPs from Trinamool’s breakaway faction, the newly formed Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) are also attending the alliance meeting.

. Young cyclist Harshita Jakhar rode into history books by becoming the first Indian woman to be a part of the Tour de France Femmes in Switzerland. The 19-year-old led a pack of eight talented cyclists from Afghanistan, Algeria, Chile, Ethiopia with two riders, Namibia and Uganda during the ceremonial start at Stage 2 of the gruelling race yesterday. The event started on 1st of this month in Lausanne and will end on 9th August in Nice.The team, handpicked by UCI (Union Cycliste de Internationale), cycled 4.5 kilometres on a neutralised section of the course along with some riders from the WCC Road Team.Tour de France Femmes is the women’s multi-stage cycling race that corresponds to the men’s Tour de France. It is part of the UCI Women’s World Tour calendar.UCI President David Lappartient joined the riders on the start podium before the stage and expressed his delight at seeing an Indian in the mix.Hailing from Rajasthan, Harshita has been making waves on the Indian cycling circuit, sweeping almost all the medals on offer in junior category and winning regularly in the seniors section as well. Her aim is to finish among the Top 10 at the 2026 Asian Games, and win a medal in the 2030 Games.

. President Droupadi Murmu today interacted with a group of grassroots innovators from the Atal Innovation Mission at Rashtrapati Bhavan and witnessed their innovations in an exhibition. During the meeting, the President emphasised that grassroots innovations are well-suited to society’s needs, as they combine local experience, scientific thinking, and individual creativity with a sense of social responsibility. President Murmu also appreciated the efforts of the innovators for working with conviction despite challenges to bring about positive change in the lives of individuals, families, and communities.

. The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communication and Information Technology met Meta officials in New Delhi regarding the temporary removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s video from Facebook. BJP MP and chairperson of the committee, Nishikant Dubey, criticised Meta India for removing the social media post of the Prime Minister. Talking to reporters after the meeting, Mr Dubey said that the Committee has demanded Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg to apologize for this and if he does not do so then the safe harbour protection under Section 79 should be withdrawn from him.The BJP MP also accused Meta, YouTube and X of failing to adequately address issues related to their algorithms and content moderation. He alleged that the platforms had not acted effectively against child sexual abuse material and content affecting women despite India’s strict legal framework.

. Arunachal’s para shuttler Biri Takar has clinched Double Medal at BWF Para World Circuit in Brazil. Takar has won Gold in Men’s Doubles and Bronze in Men’s Singles. Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Pema Khandu congratulated the sportsman for his international achievements.Congratulating the athlete, Chief Minister in a social media post highlighted that Takar is a beneficiary of the Chief Minister’s Award to Champion Excellence in Sports (CM ACES) programme.  and said his international success reflects the programme growing impact on nurturing sporting talent in the state.

. The situation in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK) remained tense after reports of violent clashes between protesters and security forces, with rights groups alleging a significant rise in casualties. According to data updated by the Human Rights Council of Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir as of yesterday, a total of 80 fatalities have been documented.Amid the ongoing developments, the Joint Awami Action Committee has appealed to the United Nations, the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch, international media organisations, and diplomatic missions to examine available footage, and press for an immediate, independent, and impartial investigation into the violence.

. The 2026 Commonwealth Games will come to a close with a spectacular closing ceremony at the iconic Hydro Arena in Glasgow tonight. The ceremony will begin at 1:30 am Indian Standard Time and will celebrate eleven days of sporting excellence, friendship and cultural diversity. On the occasion, Ahmedabad will receive the Commonwealth Games flag and the Host Baton in a ceremonial handover during the closing ceremony, marking India as the host for the centenary 2030 edition.India’s impressive campaign at the Games, highlighted by a record-breaking performance in boxing, historic success in judo, milestone achievements in para sports and multiple medals in athletics, propelled the country to fourth place in the overall medal standings with 13 gold, 17 silver and 9 bronze medals.The closing ceremony at Glasgow’s famous Hydro arena, which holds up to 13,000 fans, will bring eleven days of athletic competition to a finale. The event, which is primarily a celebration of athlete performances, also acts as a thank you to the numerous volunteers and presents the hosts for the last time with performances by cultural organizations and community groups. The official transfer to the 24th Commonwealth Games in Amdavad in 2030 will also take place during the event.The event will be headlined by Scottish rock band Simple Minds. BEMZ, Cammy Barnes and Sandi Thom will also perform, while Australian singer Delta Goodrem will be making her third appearance at a Commonwealth Games ceremony. From India, Rashmika Mandanna and Shankar Mahadevan will headline India’s cultural showcase in Glasgow. Doordarshan will broadcast the ceremony LIVE for the fans.

. Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal met Uzbekistan’s Minister of Investment, Industry and Trade Laziz Kudratov in New Delhi today.  In a social media post, Mr Goyal said that during their meeting, they had productive discussions on further strengthening the India-Uzbekistan Strategic Partnership by enhancing cooperation in trade, investment, pharmaceuticals, connectivity, digital technologies and manufacturing. Mr Goyal expressed confidence that the growing partnership between the two nations will unlock new opportunities for businesses and contribute to shared prosperity.

. The second edition of Handloom Hackathon 2.0 – Weaving Innovations has concluded at IIT Delhi. Organised in collaboration with the Ministry of Textiles, the Hackathon was aimed at harnessing technology, design, entrepreneurship and sustainable solutions to strengthen India’s handloom sector.The Hackathon provided a national platform for innovators, researchers, faculty members and handloom experts to address challenges relating to loom modernisation, design innovation, sustainability, market access and weaver livelihoods through technological interventions. The Textile Ministry said that the Hackathon attracted over 2,500 participants.These participants included 280 participants representing the top hundred shortlisted teams from across the country to develop technology-driven solutions for the country’s handloom sector. The winning solutions given in the hackathon included AI-enabled platforms for weaver livelihoods, digital market access tools and other technology-driven innovations for loom modernisation and design.

. Vice President C P Radhakrishnan has congratulated Narender Berwal on winning the Silver Medal in the Men’s plus 90 kilogram boxing event at the Commonwealth Games. He also congratulated Gulveer Singh on securing the Bronze Medal in the Men’s 5 thousand meter event. In a social media post, the Vice President said that Gulveer Singh’s historic feat of becoming the first Indian athlete to win medals in both the men’s 5 thousand meter and 10 thousand meter events at a single Commonwealth Games edition makes this achievement even more special. He noted that these outstanding achievements are a testament to their dedication, perseverance and sporting excellence. Mr Radhakrishnan wished them continued success and many more laurels for the nation.

. The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) has facilitated the first-ever air shipment of Neelam and Totapuri mangoes from Karnataka to the Maldives. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry has said, the mango export initiative delivers over 50 per cent higher returns to farmers compared to conventional market channels. It added that the export marks a significant milestone in promoting Karnataka’s late-season mango varieties in international markets and further strengthening India’s mango export basket.Neelam mango is widely appreciated for its sweet, juicy pulp, rich aroma and suitability for desserts, smoothies and beverages, while Totapuri mango is known for its distinctive shape, sweet-tangy flavour and versatility for both fresh consumption and processing. Harvested from late June to the end of July, these late-season varieties offer an opportunity to extend India’s mango export season and cater to international demand beyond the peak harvest period.

. India’s coal production has witnessed a growth of 7.51 percent in July 2026, compared to the same period last year. The Ministry of Coal informed that the overall coal production in the country during July this year has reached 69.75 million tonnes as per provisional data. It added that the coal dispatch during the last month showed a growth of 17.34 percent year on year in July. The cumulative coal production up to July, in financial year 2026-27 stood at 302.24 million tonnes (Provisional), while the cumulative coal dispatch reached 354.70 million tonnes (Provisional), registering a growth of 5.87 percent over the same period of last Financial Year.

The government has said that there are no dues pertaining to any of the States and Union Territories are pending under Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Scheme till date. Minister of State for Rural Development Kamlesh Paswan said in reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha that the Viksit Bharat-G RAM G) Act, 2025 came into force with effect from 1st of this month in rural areas of the entire country. He said, all States and UTs have notified the VB G RAM G Scheme and have started implementing it.Mr Paswan said, the Government continuously monitors the implementation of the VB-G RAM G Scheme through the Management Information System, regular review meetings and other appropriate mechanisms. The Minister added that the budgetary allocation of over 95 thousand crore rupees has been made for the Scheme during the Financial  year 2026-27. He added that this is among the largest ever allocation made at the Budget Estimate Stage for any rural employment scheme in the history of the country.

. The National Stock Exchange (NSE) is set to introduce a new method for closing price discovery through the Closing Auction Session (CAS) from tomorrow. The new system will change the way closing prices are determined for eligible Futures & Options (F&O) stocks in the cash market, with the aim of improving price discovery and aligning Indian markets with global practices.Under the new framework, non-F&O stocks will continue regular trading until 3:30 pm, with no change in their trading schedule. Stocks included in the F&O segment will see continuous trading until 3:15 pm, followed by the Closing Auction Session from 3:15 pm to 3:35 pm. Stock and index F&O trading will continue until 3:40 pm.This move will extend equity derivatives trading by 10 minutes, resulting in different closing times across market segments. The extension of F&O trading hours is aimed at creating a smoother link between the cash and derivatives markets, while enhancing efficiency and improving the accuracy of closing price determination.Previously, closing prices were calculated using the Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP) of trades executed during the final 30 minutes of the trading session.

. Indian Railways recorded a growth of 9 percent in freight loading in July this year as compared to the corresponding month of the previous year. It loaded 141.3 million tonnes of freight during July 2026, compared to 129.7 million tonnes in July last year. The performance reflects sustained demand across core sectors of the economy and continued efforts to improve freight logistics and operational efficiency.Further, Iron Ore loading increased by 22.2 per cent, Coal by 11.5 per cent, Food Grains by 11.5 per cent, Fertilizers by 12 per cent and Balance Other Goods by 12.1 per cent. Indian Railways stepped up domestic coal supply to power plants by 20 percent due to an increase in coal demand at thermal power plants, in July compared to the corresponding month last year. The increase in freight movement resulted in an incremental freight revenue of over one thousand one hundred crore rupees in July 2025, registering an 8 per cent growth.

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) today launched the revamped version of TRAI MyCall, a mobile application that enables telecom consumers to directly assess and report the voice-calling experience. TRAI MyCall is a citizen-centric digital platform that empowers telecom consumers to share real-time feedback on their voice-calling experience, along with relevant network parameters. The platform also strengthens evidence-based regulatory oversight by enabling TRAI to assess the Quality of Experience across telecom networks based on real consumer feedback. TRAI MyCall application can be installed on Android devices from https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.trai.my

. Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Bhupender Yadav has announced the designation of Glaw Lake in Arunachal Pradesh as India’s 101st Ramsar Site. In a social media post, the Minister described the development as an important step for biodiversity conservation, water and climate security, and sustainable livelihoods. Mr Yadav said that this pristine freshwater lake in the Eastern Himalayas is a biodiversity hotspot, nestled within the Kamlang Tiger Reserve and Wildlife Sanctuary.The Minister said that Glaw Lake is surrounded by lush vegetation, with more than 150 tree species and 49 orchid species recorded within the site and its catchment. The Minister described this as a significant milestone as the State gets its first Ramsar Site. He said that India has emerged as a global leader in wetland conservation. Mr Yadav noted that from 26 Ramsar Sites in 2014 to 101 today, the journey reflects the Government’s commitment to environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, and sustainable development. He said, every new Ramsar Site strengthens the Government’s resolve to protect nature while securing the future of communities that depend on these invaluable ecosystems.

. At least eight people were killed after Ukraine launched a large-scale overnight drone attack targeting military, energy, and civilian infrastructure across several regions of Russia. According to Russia’s Defence Ministry, its air defence systems intercepted 635 drones during the attack. Local authorities said, three people were killed and two others injured in the Udmurtia region, while three more people lost their lives and five were injured in the Belgorod region. Two fatalities were reported in another area.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, Kyiv’s forces targeted a military airbase in Engels, which houses Russian long-range bombers, as well as an oil refinery in Saratov. Ukraine also claimed that its forces struck an oil depot in Russia’s western Kaluga region and reported fires at the targeted facilities.

. The Ministry of Tourism and IndiGo have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) today, marking the beginning of a strategic collaboration to promote Incredible India Initiative. In a social media post, Union Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said that India has an extraordinary tourism story to tell, and under this partnership both the Government and IndiGo together are we are taking it to the world. He noted that the MoU marks the beginning of Incredible India by IndiGo, a strategic partnership that will leverage IndiGo’s extensive global network to showcase country’s unparalleled cultural, spiritual, natural and wellness destinations to millions of travelers worldwide.Mr Shekhawat underlined that this collaboration is another step towards strengthening Brand India and making the nation a preferred global tourism destination under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

. Spain has said the death toll in the Ceuta border crisis with Morocco has risen to 72. The victims include migrants who drowned and others who died in a stampede while attempting to cross into the Spanish enclave. In response to the unprecedented influx, Spanish authorities have begun installing a 500-metre-long containment barrier along the sea border between Ceuta and neighbouring Morocco to curb illegal crossings.Meanwhile, the European Union will hold emergency talks on Tuesday to discuss the migration crisis in Ceuta.  Twenty-two member states have issued a joint letter calling for coordinated action and the strengthening of the EU’s external borders after around 60,000 migrants entered the Spanish enclave from Morocco earlier this week. Spain’s Interior Ministry said most of the migrants have already returned to Morocco, while authorities on both sides continue efforts to restore order and address the humanitarian situation.The crisis has also prompted a wider European response. Italy has temporarily suspended open-border travel with Spain following the sharp increase in migrant crossings into Ceuta. The decision affects flights and maritime transport between the two countries and temporarily halts Spain’s participation in Italy’s implementation of the Schengen border-free travel arrangements.
